name: Luxury steel sports watch
summary: A sports watch that costs more than a gold dress watch. It has a steel case with exposed screws, a patterned dial and a bracelet that grows from the case. The Royal Oak of 1972 and the Nautilus of 1976 set the type.

philosophy.core_thesis: Steel can be luxury if the maker finishes it like gold, so the price comes from the hand work, not from the metal.
design_principles: Fuse the case and the bracelet into one flowing line, with no lug and no gap at the join.
Fix the bezel with visible screws or with a porthole shape, so that the case looks like a ship's window.
Alternate brushed and polished surfaces on every link, bevel and edge.
Cut a pattern in the dial, for example a tapisserie grid with 1 mm squares or horizontal lines.
Keep the case 7 to 10 mm thick and 39 to 42 mm wide, to wear like a dress watch.
Make the watch water resistant to 50 or 100 m, as a sports watch is.
Print baton markers and hands in the same tone as the case, with luminous fill.
Make the bracelet taper from 28 mm at the case to 18 mm at the clasp.
anti_patterns: A leather strap on an integrated case
A dial with a plain flat finish and a cheap print
A case with round lugs that stand out from the line
A thick diving case with a rotating bezel
A bracelet with a thin hollow link
A decorated case with gemstones and enamel

silhouette.shape: An octagon or a rounded cushion in steel, with an integrated bracelet that flows out of the case.
silhouette.line: One sloping line from the bezel to the bracelet; sharp bevels on each edge.
silhouette.fit: The bracelet wraps the wrist with a snug fit and the case lies flat.
silhouette.proportion: Case thickness to width about 1 to 4.5; the dial fills about 75 per cent of the face; the bracelet tapers by 10 mm.
rules: Make the bezel and the bracelet links one design, with the same bevel on both.
Use a pattern on the dial and keep the markers simple.
Make the case and bracelet in one metal, with no two-tone trim except on request.
Hide the clasp under the line of the bracelet.

fabrics.rule: Make the case and the bracelet in steel with a fine finish, and add a sapphire crystal. Keep gold for the two-tone and the precious versions.

methods: case and bracelet cut in steel
eight screws on a steel bezel
sapphire crystal with an anti-reflective layer
integrated bracelet with a hidden clasp
construction.closures: A folding clasp that lies flat closes the bracelet; a screw-down crown sets the time and seals the case.
construction.details: A patterned dial, an octagonal bezel with eight screws, a flowing bracelet and polished bevels.

surface.pattern: A tapisserie grid or a horizontal groove pattern on the dial, in one tone.
surface.gloss: Brushed steel at 20 to 40 GU; polished bevels at 85 to 95 GU; the dial at 30 to 60 GU.
surface.wear: The brushed faces scratch to a soft grey and the polished bevels hold a bright line; a service renews both.

palette.strategy: One metal, steel or white gold, with a dial in blue, grey or black as the only colour.

processes: hand bevelling and polishing of each edge
making.scale: Hand finished in small lots; the first Royal Oak ran at a few thousand pieces a year.
making.signs: An octagonal bezel with screws, a patterned dial and an integrated bracelet.

pieces.form: Octagonal steel case with eight bezel screws
Tapisserie dial in blue with baton markers
Integrated steel bracelet with polished bevels
Sapphire crystal with an anti-reflective layer
Slim white gold case with a patterned dial

emotion.target_response: A quiet certainty of status: the viewer sees a hard metal that a craftsman has worked as a jewel.

use_cases: a prop for a 1970s or modern finance scene
an image prompt for a steel watch on a wrist
avoid_when: the brief wants a gold dress watch with leather
the brief wants a plastic or digital watch
the brief wants a rugged field watch

modifiers.how: Swap the steel for plastic, print a bright pattern on the dial and use a one-piece strap.
Add a rotating bezel and a screw-down crown and raise the water resistance to 200 m.
